questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The location - I wanted to study and live in Andalucia, due to my big interest in the culture and history.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall an amazing and unforgettable experience, in a city that is very special to me now, and I can't wait to go back for a visit.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was difficult at times, but there's always people to ask for help.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an orientation day with a lot of information, and many ESN volunteers ready to help you and answer a lot of questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The assistance from the International Office and the Erasmus-coordinator could have been better, especially when answering urgent e-mails about changing courses, etc.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found my housing at Spotahome, a very good platform with a helpful support system.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Very nice to get a change of surroundings after a long day at campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was really lucky to have a nice landlord, who helped a lot with things in the apartment, if needed, and some really sweet flatmates.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process itself was okay, but unfortunately very confusing and a long process when it came to changing courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The International Office, Erasmus-coordinator and professors.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It took a lot of time and energy, but in the end it worked out.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure that you've already figured out your schedule before arriving, so that you, hopefully, won't have to change any courses, in case they overlap each other.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Some of the courses were quite interesting with great and helpful professors, but other courses didn't fit the description of the course on the university's website.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of some of the courses, and the way of teaching, was very similar to high schools in Denmark.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very different from what I'm used to at UCPH, very similar to high school and a bit too chill and not so structured in some courses.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Asignatura Fundamentos de Lingüística General
Asignatura Historia de la Lingüística
Asignatura Historia de España Contemporanea
Asignatura Historia del Mundo Actual
Asignatura Historia y Cultura de los Países Hispánicos

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would definitely recommend the course "Fundamentos de Lingüística General", due to an amazing professor in the practical part of the course, who was so helpful to us Erasmus students, and was always making sure that we understood the assignment, etc. 
I would also recommend the course "Historia de España Contemporanea", due to some very interesting topics and a really sweet professor, who made the classes even better with her amazing vibe and her way of teaching.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Non.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything were way cheaper than here in Denmark, so very pleased with that.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Those I attended were super good.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of different sports activities, language exchanges, trips, social gatherings, etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of the listed activities above - great opportunities to meet a lot of new people from all over the world.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore the city and go visit other cities, or countries, if you have the time, energy and money.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy, it came very naturally when you got settled down and got a new rutine.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open and don't be afraid to ask for help or talk with the local students, the majority is really open as well and always very nice and helpful.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I guess it had to be the fact that people were a bit too chill and slow about certain things, like paperwork or answering e-mails, or that the other students were quite disrespectful (talking a lot) and noisy during class.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How open and nice people were, and their way of living with enjoying the small, good and simple things in life.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Make sure your schedule is all good and done before arriving.
Attending the university, with all that it includes, may seem a bit confusing and overwhelming at first, but it will all work out in the end.
Enjoy your time and don't stress too much.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not that I can think of right now.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Having the opportunity to live and study in a country that's so special to me and always has been a huge interest of mine - so many amazing experiences, memories and new friendships.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being able to overcome whatever came my way and realising that I can handle and fix way more than I thought, super proud of that.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Go on exchange, it's an amazing opportunity and you won't regret it.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
